definitions.explanation: Derived from a single fertilized egg, used primarily to describe identical twins who share the same genetic material.

examples.japanese: {一卵性|いちらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}。
{二人|ふたり}は{一卵性|いちらんせい}の{双子|ふたご}だから{見分|みわ}けがつかない。
examples.english: The two are identical twins, so I can't tell them apart.

examples.japanese: {一卵性|いちらんせい}の{双子|ふたご}は{遺伝子|いでんし}が{同|おな}じだ。
examples.english: Identical twins have the same genes.

notes:
{一卵性|いちらんせい} is a scientific term meaning "monozygotic" — derived from a single fertilized egg. It is almost always used as a modifier before {双子|ふたご} or {双生児|そうせいじ}.

ETYMOLOGY:
A compound of {一|いち} (one) + {卵|らん} (egg) + {性|せい} (nature/type).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {一卵性|いちらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}: identical twins (formal/medical)
- {一卵性|いちらんせい}の{双子|ふたご}: identical twins (everyday)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一卵性|いちらんせい}: identical/monozygotic (from one egg)
- {二卵性|にらんせい}: fraternal/dizygotic (from two eggs)

USAGE:
{双子|ふたご} alone means "twins" without specifying type. {双生児|そうせいじ} is the more formal medical term for twins. In everyday conversation, {一卵性|いちらんせい}の{双子|ふたご} is more common than {双生児|そうせいじ}.
